newsitem.title: JAPAN: SKI JUMPING-POLISH YOUNGSTER DOUBLES TALLY.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-POLISH YOUNGSTER DOUBLES TALLY.

text.p: Polish teenager Adam Malysz defied tricky winds to soar to only his second World Cup victory in a normal hill competition on Saturday.
Malysz, 19, leapt 93 metres in his second try to clinch victory with a total of 239 points. His first jump of 89.5 had left him down in sixth place on Sapporo's Miyanomori jumping hill.
"You get either good or bad luck in conditions like this and fortunately I was lucky today," Malysz said of his wind-assisted second jump.
Winds gusted up to 32 kph during the event, disrupting the timing of some of Malysz's key challengers.
His only previous World Cup victory was in the final event of the 1996 series in Oslo last March.
Mika Laitinen of Finland posted the longest jump of 94 metres in the second round to share second place with Norway's Sturle Holseter, who recorded 92.5 and 90 for 234 points.

Overall World Cup leader Primoz Peterka of Slovenia did not travel to Japan for the event, Sunday's large hill competition and a two-day competition in Hakuba, a site of the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics.
